envmap.split_how: Yes — the format is deterministically parseable with a ~30-line state machine. Algorithm: scan line-by-line; a block starts at '# [host] path' (regex ^#\s\[(\w+)\]\s(.+)$) sandwiched between '# ===...' bars, followed by optional '#  ALSO [host] path' lines; body = every subsequent line matching ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=.* (plus '# NOTE:' lines, which carry real credentials and should travel with the block) until the next bar. The three footers are comment-only and contain no KEY=VALUE lines, so emitting only matched KV lines auto-excludes them. Route each block to a per-system file either (a) by source path — reuse harvest.py's own IN_SCOPE keyword matching (path contains 'sap-b1'->sapb1.env, 'hana'->hana.env, 'tankhapay'->tankhapay.env, 'ecomcliauto'->portals.env, root ~/jivo-cli/.env->apps.env) — or (b) by key prefix, which is clean because the vault's vars follow strict prefixes: SAPB1_*->sapb1, HANA_*->hana-sql, JSAP_*/OMS_*/EXIM_*/JIVO_FACTORY_*/ECOM_*/JIVO_ECOM_*->the app CLIs, TPAY_*->tankhapay, ZEPTO_*/BLINKIT_*/AMAZON_*/FLIPKART_*/GOOGLE_*->portals. Four caveats: (1) duplicate-key collisions across blocks with DIFFERENT values — TPAY_* appears in 3 blocks, HANA_* in 3 (direct vs tunnel hosts), SAPB1_* in 2 (vps MCP vs local CLI) — the splitter needs a precedence rule (harvest.py's rank(): vps first, or pick tunnel-vs-direct by target network); (2) '# NOTE:' lines hold secrets in comment form — don't strip comments blindly; (3) postsql and SSH-key material are pointer-only and can never be split out of this file — copy the referenced files separately; (4) dsr-cli has no block at all, so a 'split all-env.txt' bundle will silently lack DSR creds.

readme_must_say: THIS ZIP CONTAINS LIVE CREDENTIALS. Do not forward it, upload it to a drive/email, or leave it in Downloads; delete the zip after installing. (Daman's own rule for the bundle-builder: generated zips never get committed or publicly deployed.)
Where to unzip — Mac: your home folder, i.e. ~/jivo-cli, NOT Documents/Desktop/Downloads (macOS blocks remote-support access there). Windows: a short path without spaces, e.g. C:\jivo-cli.
Mac first run: run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine ~/jivo-cli` once, or every binary will be blocked as 'unidentified developer'; if a command says 'permission denied', `chmod +x` it.

First command, yourself, not whoever set the machine up: `python3 harness/bin/setup.py` (Windows: `python harness/bin/setup.py`) — your name and department go on your reports and route your team's rules.
Second command: your department's doctor from the SETUP.md table (e.g. Accounts Mac: ./sap-b1/cli/sapb1 doctor). Green = ready. Red = credentials or network, message Daman — do not guess.

Network: SAP and HANA answers need the office network, the FortiClient VPN, or the tunnel this kit was configured with — from plain home Wi-Fi the SAP doctor WILL fail even with perfect credentials. Everything else (sales/factory/ecom/imports/ops portals) works from any internet.
Logins expire: ecom/oms/factory/control-panel sessions last about a day — the re-login one-liners are in the root README 'Credentials & auth' section (or your box got a scheduled refresh task).

Reading is safe everywhere and changes nothing. SAP is the only writable system, only via draft/post/patch typed by you, always previewing and requiring the full word 'yes'. If a write ever says 'outcome unknown' (exit 7): STOP, do not re-run, check SAP, tell Daman.
Windows users: use `python` not `python3`; imports (exim) needs Git Bash; write payloads are easier via --data-file than escaped quotes.
Don't edit CLAUDE.md, .claude/, or harness/bin — the daily sync reverts and reports it. Don't copy your credential files anywhere else.
If an answer looks wrong, say so in the chat — corrections you make reach every other operator's copy by the next day.
